sections.title: The Foundations Every Task Must Get Right
sections.lead: Two decisions made before prompt 1 that cannot be repaired afterwards. Each one is cheap to check and expensive to get wrong.

sections.title: What you may not tell Model A or Model B
sections.lead: Leg A defines the task: the opening prompt and the follow ups you send Model A. Leg B is the golden run: Model B gets the same opening prompt, word for word, then the turns you send it as you steer it through the milestones. The no leak rule and the input folder are the same in both legs; what a turn may point at is not.

sections.title: Milestones
sections.lead: Written from the Leg A conversation with Model A, used in Leg B to steer Model B. Three standards cover what sits around the intent line: Modifier and Assets Delivered, the stopping rules, and one milestone per requirement on every Leg A turn.

sections.title: A rubric that separates two runs
sections.lead: A rubric exists to tell a strong run from a weak one. Five standards keep it doing that, and a set can break any of them while still looking complete.

sections.title: Criteria a correct run can pass
sections.lead: A criterion has to pass a correct run, fail a wrong one, carry the right Category and Evaluation Target, and count once. If your own golden fails one, check the criterion first: it is usually the one that is broken.

sections.title: The subjective block
sections.lead: Ten or more criteria, no more than 30% of the weight, each grading a property of the render rather than your golden's wording, and each naming its file when the task ships more than one. Check all four before you submit.

sections.title: Closing the task
sections.lead: The golden is a deliverable, not a run you stopped. Check every value against its source and every revision for wording it left behind, then run the close out before you submit.

mistakes.title: The deliverable sits below the complexity bar
mistakes.what: The deliverable misses its type's complexity floor. Typically the Agent Objective says dashboard, no prompt asks for interaction, and the page ships static.
mistakes.why: A page that does nothing when clicked clears neither the interactive HTML floor nor the dashboard floor. It is a document, the lowest priority deliverable on the bar, so the task falls short of what the client asked for however good the reasoning underneath is. The deliverable is set by the prompts at scenario stage, so it cannot be patched later.
mistakes.spot: Ask what the page does when someone clicks it. If nothing, it is a document, whatever the Agent Objective calls it.
mistakes.fix: Before prompt 1, check the deliverable type against its floor, and have a prompt ask for the interaction the data supports.

sources.quote: Interactive HTML: Interaction that actually works: controls that respond, state that changes, filters or navigation. A styled static page does not qualify. Dashboard: Several linked views over data the model extracted itself. One chart is not a dashboard.

mistakes.title: The task relies on records the universe does not hold
mistakes.what: A rule reads off records the assigned universe does not hold, such as a catalog or a policy page, while prompts, inputs and criteria read as if they were there.
mistakes.why: A rule pointing at data no tool returns cannot be followed by any run, so every criterion downstream of it is unreachable. Not wrong. Impossible. It takes the difficulty with it too: if that data was the second system the task cross checks against, every cross check has nothing on the other side, and the task is no longer multi system.
mistakes.spot: Your golden shows it: an empty search, a Leg B hint sending Model B another way, figures flagged as unconfirmed.
mistakes.fix: Before the run, query the universe once per rule and rewrite any rule whose record is missing. If it only surfaces in Leg B, redesign the task rather than hint again.

rows.text:
Updated **`/app/outputs/pantry_audit.html`** (v2). Here's what changed and why.

## First, the honest blocker
I did go to Fresh directly on your account this time — but the two endpoints that serve product pages and policy text (`search_shop_catalog` and `search_shop_policies_and_faqs`) return **zero results for everything**, including items I can prove are in your catalog (I searched Sourdough loaf, Jasmine rice, Romano, Gala apples, 2% milk — all things you've ordered — and all came back empty). The account itself is fine (profile, history, cart, subscriptions all work), and the cart *does* return real Fresh price/pack data — but only for a variant ID that's already in your history, and **none of the five pantry items are**. So I can't open their live pages, and I won't dress Tom's numbers up as Fresh's.

## You were right about the kept claims
Checking each claim against the rule-7 standard ("Fresh's *catalog or policies* back it" — a photo label or a nutrition line doesn't count), **three claims I kept in v1 shouldn't have been**:

- **Spinach "pre-washed"** → that's off the packaging, not Fresh's catalog copy → **removed** until the listing shows it.
- **Eggs "free-range / Grade A"** → unverifiable → **removed** (not just flagged).
- **Avocado "Organic"** → I'd kept it outright; it's actually **can't-verify** from Fresh. It matters because it's the *only* thing 2A ends up receiving, so it now carries a hard "confirm on Fresh" gate.

The ones I removed in v1 (potassium, vitamin C, 30-day return, spinach "organic") were correctly removed. Net result: **once you require Fresh to back each line, the compliant cards carry no descriptive claims at all right now** — just name, pack, price/unit — and a claim only goes back on after you see it on the product's Fresh page. There's a full claim-by-claim table in section 1.

## What's solid vs. provisional
- **Final** (rules + sheet + photo + your card statement): all verdicts are **Fix**; the per-apartment *quantities*; 2A's dropped items; 5D's "any is fine" override; the S&S logic; delivery must be split proportionally, not evenly.
- **Provisional / `Pull from Fresh`**: every price, the delivery fee/threshold, the avocado organic flag and single-vs-bag pack, and therefore the dollar amounts. The owed figures are shown with Tom's numbers only as placeholders and clearly tagged, plus one new subtlety — the S&S "2 lb" depends on Fresh's real banana price ($1.02 ÷ price/lb), so that's on the checklist too.

Section 4 is a short "confirm on Fresh before you publish" list so that when those endpoints come back (or you check the app), you can drop in real values and the numbers finalize. Want me to keep retrying the catalog endpoint, or take a run at pulling the delivery/return policy specifically?

items.text:
# 123 Main St shared pantry - group order rules
(what we agreed at the June building meeting)

1. We charge what Fresh charges us for what actually goes in the cart. Every line is priced at the pack option we add to the cart from Fresh's catalog. If an item has no pack options, use its catalog price.
2. For each item we buy the cheapest mix of Fresh's pack options that covers everyone's total. Never less than what people asked for.
3. "Organic only" apartments only get items that Fresh's own catalog marks as organic. Anything else they asked for is dropped, not swapped. Whatever an apartment said last is what counts.
4. 4B's Subscribe & Save: whatever it's due to bill in the week the order goes in (our weeks run Monday to Sunday) comes off 4B's request for that item.
5. The building account is not Prime, so no member prices or member deals. For the delivery fee we go by Fresh's Delivery Policy and nothing else.
6. Splitting: a line's cost is split by how many units each apartment gets on that line, each share rounded to the cent (if the rounded shares don't add up to the line cost, the difference goes on whoever has the most units on that line). An apartment's items total is the sum of its line shares. Each apartment's delivery share = delivery fee x (its items total / everyone's items totals added up), rounded to the cent only at the very end. Any leftover cent, up or down, goes on 4B.
7. Listing cards show: name, the pack option we're buying, price per unit (line cost / total units on that line, 2 decimals), and only claims that Fresh's own catalog or policies back up.
8. Verdicts: publish = card is right as is, fix = card needs changes, pull = nobody ends up ordering it.

mistakes.title: A Leg B hint that hands Model B the answer
mistakes.what: In Leg B, a turn you send Model B hands it what it had to work out: a value, a count, a position or the conclusion. Naming the exact file to open costs points instead.
mistakes.why: The no leak rule covers every turn you type in Leg B, exactly as in Leg A, and a leak fails the task however late it comes. A golden that meets a criterion because Model B was told the answer no longer shows the reasoning the criterion grades, and a hint that settles what one of your negatives exists to test tells Model B how to avoid the trap. What differs from Leg A is what a turn is for: a Leg B hint says what is still missing, while in Leg A a punctual correction is fine when it comes up naturally, as long as it does not compromise the 50% failure threshold.
mistakes.spot: For each Leg B turn, ask what is left for Model B to work out. A turn that states what a criterion grades has answered it.
mistakes.fix: Hint as the user would: say what looks wrong and point at the area, never at the file, the value or the conclusion. If Model B still misses, hint again at the same level.

mistakes.title: A requirement nothing grades, and a criterion nothing asked for
mistakes.what: A prompt requirement no criterion checks, or a criterion no turn asked for, usually written from the golden. Both are Major; a non critical gap, or a criterion that only narrows a real ask, costs points.
mistakes.why: An ungraded requirement means a run can do the wrong thing and still pass the whole set, which is exactly the failure the rubric existed to catch. A criterion nobody asked for does the reverse: it punishes a run for doing what the user actually said. The first is Major when the requirement is critical. The second is Incorrect Criteria, which is Major, when no turn asks for anything like it, and Overfitting, which is Moderate, when it narrows a real ask, such as an order nobody requested. It also hides: it is usually written from the golden, so the golden passes it.

mistakes.fix: Write criteria from the prompt, never from the golden. Where an instruction closes a set, write the closure: X consists only of A, B and C.

# Cleaning the Inspection Batch — Runbook

**For:** Cyrus · **From:** Anselm · **Use with:** `cleaning_walkthrough.mp4` (same steps, narrated)

> **Request:** 2024 Q4 building inspection records
> **City reference #:** 2026-1642 — City of Richmond Records Office (L. Whitfield-Baptiste)
> **Requested / acknowledged:** 2026-08-04
> **Due from the city:** ~**Tue 2026-08-25** (15 business days from acknowledgment) — i.e. the **last week of August**, per the records-office email.

This runbook exists so you can clean that batch **without me**.

---

## The one thing to internalize first

Every batch so far has come back with **the columns shuffled** — renamed, reordered, or one field split into two. So this is **not** "clean column E, then column H." If you memorize positions or names, the next export breaks you.

Instead, every step below is written as a **rule about the *role* a field plays**, not the label the city happened to print this quarter:

- Don't think *"PARCEL_ID."* Think *"the field that identifies the building."*
- Don't think *"RESULT."* Think *"the field that says how the inspection came out."*

Two habits carry the whole thing:

1. **Find each field by what it *contains*, then verify the header matches — never trust position.**
2. **A schema guard runs *before* any cleaning.** If this file doesn't look like last quarter's, we want to know *before* the cleaners silently mangle it — not after it's in a chart.

And one rule that overrides "make it tidy":

3. **Flag, don't fill.** When something is missing or ambiguous, we mark it for review. We do **not** invent it. (The crossed-out "backfill blank permits by hand" on my sketch was a bad idea — ignore it.)

Pipeline, from the sketch: **Load → Normalize → Dedupe → Validate → Export.** The guard lives at the front of Load. **Geocoding is not in this pipeline** — that's Wren's separate pass, downstream, after we hand off a clean file.

---

## Step 1 — Load & Schema Guard  *(the check that runs before the cleaners)*

**Goal:** refuse to proceed if the file doesn't match the shape we expect.

**Load rule:** read the CSV **by header name into a dictionary per row**, never by column index. Column order is allowed to change between batches; our code must not care.

**Guard — trip any of these and STOP, don't clean:**

- **Missing role.** For each role we need (building id, address, district, permit, inspection type, inspection subtype, inspection date, result, inspector, violations count, zip, inspection id), a column must be locatable. If a role can't be found → **stop and ask**, the city renamed or dropped it.
- **A field that used to be one is now two (or two became one).** This *already happened*: inspection type split into a **type** field and a **subtype** field (`building`/`final`, `electrical`/`rough-in`). If the count of type-ish columns changes again → **stop**. (See #C_DATATEAM, "columns shifted, inspection_type is two fields now.")
- **A brand-new column appears** that maps to no known role → **stop and ask** before assuming it's junk.
- **Content doesn't match role — the real tell that columns slid.** Sniff each field's *values*, not just its header:
  - the date field must *parse as dates*,
  - the result field must contain only outcome words,
  - the building-id field must look like parcel ids,
  - the violations field must be numbers.
  If a column's header says one thing but its values look like another, the columns shifted (this is the "parcel id sliding into the wrong column, ~900 rows" case). **Stop.**
- **Row count sanity.** Wildly off from what the city's cover note / row count says → **stop**.

Only when the guard passes do we touch the data.

---

## Step 2 — Normalize  *(fix each field by its role, not its name)*

Normalize each **role**. For every rule there's a **check** that turns a schema change into a loud failure instead of silent bad data.

### 2a. The field that identifies the building (parcel id)
- **Reality:** two shapes in one column — a long all-numeric id and a short hyphenated id — and many carry a **unit suffix** `-A` / `-B` (same building, different unit).
- **Rule:** canonicalize the format, but **keep the suffix** (it's the unit). Separately derive a **suffix-stripped "building key"** — we'll use it in dedupe.
- **Check:** every value matches one of the two known shapes. Anything else → **flag**, don't guess.

### 2b. The field that says how the inspection came out (result)
- **Rule:** lower-case to the closed set **{pass, fail, partial}**.
- **Check:** it's a **closed vocabulary**. Any value outside the set → **flag**. A new outcome word = the city changed the categories = schema drift.

### 2c. The two fields for what kind of inspection it was (type + subtype)
- **Rule:** lower-case; keep **type and subtype as a pair** (e.g. `electrical` + `rough-in`).
- **Check:** exactly these two role-fields exist. If they merge back into one, or a third appears → **stop**. *(This is the documented example of the city "improving" the export on us.)*

### 2d. The field with the inspection date
- **Reality:** three formats in the same column — `2024-10-06`, `10/18/2024`, and `20-Oct-2024`.
- **Rule:** parse **each known format explicitly** to ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Never let the parser guess an ambiguous date.
- **Check:** every value parses under one of the known patterns **and** falls inside the quarter's window (Q4 → Oct–Dec 2024). Unparseable or out-of-window → **flag, don't drop**.

### 2e. The field with the inspector's name (the "owner" column)
- **Reality:** loaded with trailing/leading whitespace (about **half** the rows last batch). Stray spaces are exactly what makes a name fail to match a lookup later.
- **Rule:** strip leading/trailing whitespace and collapse internal doubles.
- **Check:** after cleaning, `value == value.strip()` for every name (no residual leading/trailing space), and every name maps to the **known roster**; an unknown inspector → **flag**. And **every row must have an inspector** — a blank owner is the thing that bites us downstream, so flag it. **This is where the June crash gets stopped:** after the strip, also assert the **distinct count doesn't drop when you strip** (a hidden space silently splits one person into two). June died on `hours[row["INSPECTOR"]] += 1` → **`KeyError: 'D. Salazar '`** — a single trailing space on the inspector field broke an aggregation keyed on the raw value. Fixing it here, where the whitespace is stripped, is what stops it. *(And never key a count/join on a raw text field — key on the normalized value.)*

### 2f. The field with the district / neighborhood
- **Reality:** case variants (`The Fan` vs `the fan`) and a catch-all `RVA` that isn't a real neighborhood.
- **Rule:** map to the **canonical neighborhood list** (title-case + alias map).
- **Check:** closed vocabulary. `RVA` and anything not on the canonical list → **flag for review**, don't silently coerce it into a real neighborhood.

### 2g. The field with the permit number  — **flag, don't fill**
- **Reality:** mixed formats (`BLD-2024-03386`, `BLD-2024-3314`, bare `3521`) **and blanks**.
- **Rule:** where a real number exists, normalize to the canonical `BLD-YYYY-#####`. Where it's **blank, leave it blank and flag the row.** Do **not** fabricate a permit number. *(This is the crossed-out sketch item — the answer is flag, not fill.)*
- **Check:** every non-blank value matches the permit shape; blanks are **counted and surfaced**, never invented.

### 2h. The field with the zip — **flag, don't fill**
- **Rule:** keep as-is. **Blank zip → flag.** Don't back-derive it from the address (same flag-don't-fill principle; a wrong zip is worse than a missing one).
- **Check:** every non-blank zip is 5 digits and in the Richmond set.

### 2i. The field with the violations count
- **Rule:** coerce to integer.
- **Check:** numeric and ≥ 0; blank or negative → **flag**.

### 2j. The field with the street address
- **Rule:** light touch only — trim, and standardize the suite tokens (`STE 200 REAR`) against the **city address-standard reference table** (Wren dropped it in the project folder for the permits story). **Do not geocode here.**
- **Check:** non-empty after trim.

---

## Step 3 — Dedupe

- **Exact duplicate rows** (whole-row repeats): drop. Keep one.
- **Same inspection id repeated:** collapse to one **only if the rest of the row agrees**. If an id repeats with a **conflicting** field (e.g. the same inspection under `E1350-114` and `E1350-114-B`), that's the suffix case — reconcile on the **building key**, keep one, and **flag the conflict**.
- **Building-level duplicates from `-A`/`-B` suffixes:** strip the suffix to the building key and dedupe on that so the units collapse. **As a backstop, dedupe on `address + inspection date`** — that's the key we settled on in the thread. *(Last time this collapsed ~40 flagged dupes down to ~14 real ones — don't over-drop, verify.)*
- **Cross-batch overlap:** dedupe against **batches 1–3** on inspection id so multi-quarter cases aren't double-counted; **flag** repeat inspections rather than silently merging them (we don't want to double-count violations).
- **Null building ids:** **do not drop.** Some are demolitions with no street address — legitimately null. Put them in a **separate bucket** and keep them.

---

## Step 4 — Validate  *(before export — this is where totals must tie out)*

- **Row accounting closes.** `rows_in = rows_out + exact_dups_removed + collapsed_dups + null_bucket + flagged_pulled`. Every input row is somewhere. Nothing silently vanished.
- **The count the dedupe step *reported* equals the count actually removed.** (Totals tie out to the batch — the same sign-off you gave last batch when you checked the cleaning notebook.)
- **Closed-vocabulary re-check** on result, type/subtype, and district — nothing slipped through as a stray value.
- **Every date** parsed and in-window; **every violations** value numeric; **every row has an inspector.**
- **Flag summary printed:** N blank permits, N blank zips, N unknown districts, N unknown inspectors, N null parcels, N id conflicts. All non-zero flags are **surfaced, none filled.** If any flag bucket is unexpectedly huge, that's a schema-drift signal — go back to the guard.

---

## Step 5 — Export

- Write the cleaned file with a **stable, canonical column order** that *we* define — so nothing downstream ever depends on the order the city sent.
- Write a companion **`*_flags.csv`** (or a `review` sheet): every flagged row plus the reason, for the hand-review pile.
- Write a short **run report**: rows in, rows out, dropped, bucketed, flagged — so the next person can eyeball in ten seconds that totals tie out.
- Hand off the clean file. **Geocoding happens after this, separately** (Wren's QGIS pass). It is not our step.

---

## When a check trips — what to do

1. **Don't "fix" it in the cleaner.** A tripped guard means the *file* changed, not that the data is dirty.
2. Look at the failing field's **values** and decide which role it really is.
3. If the city renamed/re-split a field, **update the role-to-header mapping in one place** (the schema map), not scattered through the code.
4. If something is missing or ambiguous, **flag it** and move on. We never fill.
5. If you're unsure whether it's a story-affecting change, ping me — but the batch can still be cleaned and handed off with the ambiguous rows flagged.

*Sources behind these rules: the pipeline sketch, the 09-04 standup voice note, the #C_DATATEAM cleaning threads (batches 1–3), and a profile of the last raw Q4 export.*

The assistant must build one index of the practice's job history out of all four sources and reconcile them against each other: the 23 ranch and boundary jobs in the handwritten ledger covering 2011 to 2025, the 468 invoices in the QuickBooks export covering the same years and including the town work that never entered the ledger, the eight county filing receipts, and the current year's jobs, which were never written on paper and exist only in the firm's own mail, calendar and bank records. Job 16-058 must enter that index on the ledger alone because it has no invoice row, and invoice 21-018 must enter it on the export alone because it has no ledger line.

The assistant must run the conflict check for Cause No. 26-0402-CV against every party named in that matter, being Speegle Family Partnership, Ltd., Panhandle Ag Holdings, LP and Cudahy Sand and Gravel, Inc., and against the tract at issue, the common line between Section 14 and Section 15, Block K-3, D. & P. Ry. Co. Survey, Deaf Smith County. Eight engagements must come back. 26-004 for Panhandle Ag Holdings, LP is a current-year engagement for a named adverse party and bars acceptance. 19-034, entered as "Panhandle Agric. Hldgs" on 5-21-19 in Deaf Smith County over the SW/4 of Section 15 Block K-3 at $3,250, is the same party and matches on both party and tract. 22-012, Panhandle Ag Holdings LP, 2-14-22, Castro County, Section 44 Block M-7, $2,400, matches on party only, as do 18-030 for Cudahy Sand and Gravel Inc on 5-08-18 and 25-019 for Cudahy Sand & Gravel on 3-24-25, both in Oldham County over Section 3 Block 9 at $3,900 and $4,300, the second being the same party as the first. 12-017 for Orval Speegle, 4-09-12, Deaf Smith County, N/2 of Section 14 Block K-3, $1,900, comes back on the tract and is tied to Speegle Family Partnership, Ltd. by surname and by the billing address they share in the invoice export. 24-028 for Speegle Family Partnership, Ltd. on 6-03-24, same ground, $2,100, is prior work for the party on his own side and matches on party and tract. 20-009 for Hereford Feeders, Inc., 2-19-20, Deaf Smith County, S/2 of Section 14 Block K-3, $2,750, comes back on the tract alone with no party overlap at all.

The assistant must report that the offered engagement cannot be accepted, and the reason must be 26-004, grounded in the firm's own current records rather than in anything on paper: a boundary and topographic survey of a 640-acre pivot tract in Deaf Smith County, flown on 2026-06-10 and again on 2026-06-24 against PO 26-1140, with $18,400.00 received on 2026-07-09, and no record anywhere that the as-built surface and the coverage exhibit were ever delivered.

Three records must be kept out of that run. 15-022 for Hereford Feeders Inc sits in Section 22 Block K-2, a different block from the Block K-3 at issue. 17-052 for Panhandle Air and the Panhandle Land Title invoices are separate entities from Panhandle Ag Holdings, LP and share nothing with it but the first word of the name.

The assistant must then run the same check for Cause No. 26-0114-CV against Threadgill Ranch Partners, Ltd., Bertrand Sisemore and Sisemore Cattle Co., and against the common line between Section 21 and Section 22, Block 4-T, T.&N.O. Ry. Co. Survey, Moore County. Nine prior engagements for Bertrand Sisemore and Sisemore Cattle Co. must come back, not the eight disclosed on 2026-03-11. The ninth is 16-058, entered in the ledger on 4-19-16 as "B. D. Sisemore" in Moore County with no description and a fee of n/c, and absent from the invoice export because it was never billed. Its party and its ground both come from Moore County receipt 16-0771, filed 2016-04-22 for $34.00, which names the instrument as "Monument record, W line Sec 22, Blk 4-T, T.&N.O. Ry. Co. Sur." and the party as Sisemore Cattle Co. The west line of Section 22 is the common line in dispute, so 16-058 touched it.

Both consequences of that finding must be stated. The disclosure of 2026-03-11 is incomplete at nine engagements rather than eight, and its sentence "None of the eight touched the common line between Section 21 and Section 22, Block 4-T" is contradicted by 16-058. That run must also return 20-061 for Threadgill Ranch Partners Ltd, 9-30-20, Sherman County, Section 4 Block 2-B, $1,400, as prior work for his own client, disclosable but not a bar, and it must keep out 13-051 for Sizemore Trucking in Hutchinson County, which is a different party from Sisemore Cattle Co.

The dates must be reconciled to a single basis and that basis must be stated. 15-091 is entered in the ledger on 9-28-15 but appears in the 2026-03-11 disclosure as 2015-10-09, which receipt 15-2244 shows is the date its plat was filed rather than the date the job came in.

Exactly three records must be listed as unresolved rather than cleared, each with the reason it cannot be closed, and none of the three may be reported as cleared. 14-011 for Kalbfleisch Feedyard, 3-27-14, Deaf Smith County, $2,200, has no description in the ledger and nothing was ever filed on it. 21-018 is a $450.00 retainer invoice dated 2021-03-04 to "D.S. CO." with no billing address, no telephone, no job number and no ledger line, so neither the party nor the county can be established. And the tract covered by 26-004 was never written down anywhere, so while the party is certain from three separate sources the ground is not.

Every identification of one party appearing under two spellings must carry the evidence that produced it, drawn from the records rather than from resemblance: the billing address and telephone number the two spellings share in the invoice export, the party as named on the filed instrument in the receipt book, and the matching contact record. Names that merely look alike must be held apart on the same evidence, so that Sizemore Trucking LLC of Borger stays separate from Sisemore Cattle Co. of Dumas, and Panhandle Land Title and Panhandle Air stay separate from Panhandle Ag Holdings, LP.

One disclosure paragraph must be produced per run, built from the index and nothing else. Each must name the job numbers and the dates it relies on, and each must say which records remain unresolved instead of leaving them out. The second must also say whether the March disclosure still stands and, if it does not, what has to go out before the pretrial conference.

All of it must be delivered in a single self-contained interactive HTML file named conflict_check.html, revised in place at every turn rather than replaced, holding both completed runs at the end with the second not displacing the first, and opening straight from the local file with no network request. The page must work as a tool rather than read as a report: a control that runs the check against a party name or a tract, typed or selected; a filter across cleared, disclose, bars and unresolved that actually changes what is shown; the evidence and the source of each fact on every row, with each job's full record expandable; and a header giving the matter, the cause number, the court and the date the check was run.

The clearing rules and the user's standing preferences must be carried to persistent memory, so the check can be run again in a later session without starting over. And everything established in earlier turns must survive each revision, unless that revision asked for it to change.

This year is not something I am going to export for you. It is in my mail, my calendar and the bank.

Different matter. The one I am already in. Cause No. 26-0114-CV, 69th District Court of Moore County, Threadgill Ranch Partners, Ltd. against Sisemore Cattle Co. Wendell is for Threadgill. The line is the common line between Section 21 and Section 22, Block 4-T, T. and N.O. Ry. Co. Survey.

## What I added: the change-board decision step (scene 14)

A new scene, **"Three decisions, not one,"** shows that **finding a discrepancy, accepting a change request, and releasing a changed figure are three separate decisions** — grounded in the status history around the same three cases:

- **Decision 1 — Find the discrepancy** *("Is there a discrepancy?")* → 26 May flight line: **3 found**. Raise it, don't quietly fix.
- **Decision 2 — Accept the change request** *("Do we make this change?")* → at the board: **accepted / deferred / returned** (e.g. **32-21-07 accepted (Jul); a 29-11-06 Fig 12 request deferred**).
- **Decision 3 — Release the changed figure** *("Does it ship — and when?")* → **figure freeze 25 Sep → quarterly revision to Meridian 30 Sep**. Accepted is not released.

Banner + narration drive the point home: *finding ≠ accepting ≠ releasing — three decisions, three records.* Each data point is drawn straight from the Slack/email record, and I kept the framing within what the evidence establishes (I don't claim a specific PCR *is* one of the May corrections — just that the status history *around* these figures shows all three decision types).

## Everything preserved
- **Both learning activities** intact — the predict-and-check on view reading (scenes 10–12) and the closing find-the-problem exercise (scenes 15–17).
- The **three flight-line cases** (scene 3), the **separate work-email record** with its evidence-bounded framing (scene 4), and the **full FAA leader definition / both panel headers** all unchanged.

mistakes.title: Category and Evaluation Target filled with the wrong kind of value
mistakes.what: Category or Evaluation Target does not fit the criterion: Agent Behavior or Tool Use on an artifact, a category in the target field, or a subjective row tagged Instruction Following.
mistakes.why: Category says what kind of check it is; target says where the grader looks. Both go to the client with the rubric data, so a wrong pair is wrong data even when the criterion is right. In the subjective block Task Completion is the only valid category, because anything the prompt explicitly asked for belongs in the objective block by definition.

mistakes.what: Subjective criteria describe features without naming the file that carries them, usually after the first one or two.
mistakes.why: The evaluation target only says Final Answer Artifact, not which file. Once a task ships two deliverables, or a revision turn produces a second file, “the table” or “each scene” stops identifying anything, and two graders can score the same run against different files. With a single deliverable the file is implied, and the QC appendix accepts a criterion that leaves it out as long as another criterion checks the file exists. Purpose: track where each album stands and the rules, across stints.

Scope: **laptop → T7 (verified Aug 17) AND T7 → mini (verified Aug 19).** Both passes are now in. The wipe decision is on the table.

## Which screenshot is which device
- **Laptop (source of truth), Aug 16 2026:** list view (sizes + modified dates), icon view (item counts, 8 folders), and the finale folder open (6 items). Path `Macintosh HD > Users > brandon > Videos > HoopHighlights`. 41 GB free.

Samsung T7 Shield 4TB, Amazon #113-8842061-4470258: placed May 4, shipped May 5, **delivered Wed May 6** (email). T7 volume Created May 6 7:12 PM (Get Info). Both agree.

2. verify T7: every album, item **count AND size** match laptop
3. T7 → mini

mistakes.title: Too few subjective criteria, or too much weight on them
mistakes.what: The subjective block holds fewer than ten criteria, or more than 30% of the total weight. Either alone is the error.
mistakes.why: The cap keeps the score dominated by deterministic checks. Over it, presentation judgments start to crowd out whether the task was done. Under the count, the block cannot cover a multi panel deliverable: a nested table, a timeline strip or a set of diagrams goes ungraded, and two runs presenting the same correct figures very differently score the same.
mistakes.spot: Count the rows, ten at least, and divide the subjective weight by the total, signs ignored.
mistakes.fix: Add a criterion for each region nothing grades. Over the cap, add the objective checks your prompts call for, then lower overstated subjective weights.

Status labels are distinguishable without relying on colour alone, each carrying a word as well as a swatch.
Each question sits with the item it arises from, rather than only in a separate list at the end.

Dates are rendered in one consistent format across the page.
Section boundaries are marked by a visible rule or panel edge, not by whitespace alone.
A table on the page requires horizontal scrolling to read its rightmost column at normal window width.
Every status label offered in the page's filter control also appears on at least one item in the page.

Everything runs: the matrix generates 42 school-year weeks, all 10 month calendars render, and collision cells light up correctly. The `ctx.SCH` error is just my test harness reaching a block-scoped `const` — the builders themselves executed fine and reference it without issue.

## What I read off IMG_0814 (Jaylen's calendar)

I cropped and enlarged every month to read the marks precisely, then cross-checked against the calendar's own holiday footer:

- **Carline mornings** (yellow highlight, 7:15–7:35 AM): every **Thursday + Friday** school day. After removing Labor Day, Fall Break (Oct 9–12), Thanksgiving, Winter Break, MLK, Presidents', Spring Break, Easter (Mar 29–Apr 2), and the May 21 last day → **71 mornings** (37 Thursdays, 34 Fridays).
- **Custody handovers** (red circles, "Terrance – Poplarville" 13:30/15:30 in the margin): **7**, all Fridays, biweekly — **Aug 7 & 21, Sep 4 & 18, Oct 2, 16 & 30**. Those are the only ones circled on the sheet (Nov–May had no circles), so that's what I counted.

## The exact collision numbers

Travel days aren't on the calendar, so I made them the interactive control. The decisive fact: **100% of your carline mornings and handovers fall on Thursday or Friday.** So the count is entirely about whether the regional travel block hits those two days:

| Travel block | Carline collisions | Handover collisions |
|---|---|---|
| Front-loaded · **Mon–Wed** | **0 / 71** | **0 / 7** |
| Mid-week · **Tue–Thu** (default) | **37 / 71** | **0 / 7** |
| Back-loaded · **Wed–Fri** | **71 / 71** | **7 / 7** |

So, concretely: at 3 travel days/week, if the block ever includes **Thursday you lose 37 school mornings**; add **Friday and it's all 71 mornings plus every one of the 7 Poplarville handovers**. Only a strictly Mon–Wed block keeps both at zero.

## What I added to dashboard.html

A new **"Schedule conflict"** section (financial dashboard untouched above it):
- **Weekday travel selector + presets** (Mon–Wed / Tue–Thu / Wed–Fri), defaulting to Tue–Wed–Thu — everything recomputes live.
- **KPI cards**: 71 carline mornings, 7 handovers, and live carline/handover collision counts with %.
- **Collisions-by-pattern table** (the three presets side by side).
- **Week-by-week matrix** — all 42 school weeks, Mon–Fri, each cell tagged C / H / T with collisions filled red (holiday days greyed, "marked-but-closed" days flagged `*`).
- **Conflict calendar** — all 10 months as mini-grids: carline shaded amber, handovers ringed, travel days blue, collisions red.

The assumptions panel documents the extraction rules and holiday removals. One honest flag carried in the UI: handovers were only circled Aug–Oct on your sheet, so the 7 is what's *marked* — if custody actually continues biweekly all year, the Friday exposure is larger, which the Wed–Fri preset already hints at.

rows.text: The S6 came back from Lubbock in july and i ran it on  the baseline behind the shop the same afternoon, same as I do with anything that has been off the property. It passed . I want a short video the office can follow without me , saved as baseline_check.mp4 , and the script for it as baseline_check_script.md so Rosalba can print it and keep it in the case. It is for Estefana first and whoever comes after her. Open with where the baseline came from and what the S6 was on the bench for , then run the check end to end on my setup, and at every step show a good reading next to a bad one. Do the arithmetic on the screen , not in a spreadsheet afterwards. Feet to three places all the way through, nobody here reads millimetres. End with a set of readings they have to call before the video calls it, and the call has to be the one I would make. I will dig out the page for that. Attached are the pages from my book , the sheet came back in the case, and a photo of the setup. The sheet is nice to have . The sheet is not the check .Abe

Dug out the April page, it is attached. That is what the S6 was reading before it went in, so that is your bad one. Put the real numbers in where you had to make some up and leave everything else where it is, it is right.

This is the one for the end, attached. Loaner S5 from Llano, June, before I let it out on a job. I cut my arithmetic and my call off the bottom of the page on purpose. Show them the page, give them ten seconds, then work it on the screen and call it.

Estefana watched it twice and came back with one question, which is more than I got from anyone else: why do we not just use the number on Talmadge's sheet. Fair question. Put it in, his number worked out on the 812 next to mine, and one line on which one we use and why. One more thing while that is open, add the baseline number and my rule to MEMORY.md so next time nobody has to go looking for the book.

rows.text:
Done, Abe. Both files are in `/app/outputs`:

- **`baseline_check.mp4`** — 1080p, 1:45, plays anywhere (H.264/yuv420p, verified clean).
- **`baseline_check_script.md`** — the print-and-keep-in-the-case version, matches the video step for step.
- (Also left `make_baseline_video.py` so the video can be rebuilt when you swap in your quiz page.)

**What the video does, in your order:**
1. **Where the baseline came from** — BL-1→BL-2, published **812.000 ft**, BL-M midpoint at 406.000. "Judge against this. Not the brochure."
2. **What the S6 was on the bench for** — LEIS pulled the angles *and* the distance guts back into spec (HA collimation −19.4″→+0.6″, EDM additive −1.7mm→+0.2mm, EDM scale +2.6→+0.5ppm). Ends on "the sheet is nice to have, the sheet is not the check."
3. **Setup** — tripod both ends, over your actual photo; good vs. a pole.
4. **Step 1 PPM** — good `812.005` (PPM +52) next to bad `811.962` (PPM 0), with the math on screen: `812 × 0.000052 = 0.042 ft short`.
5. **Step 2 three sets** — tight spread (0.002, keep all) next to an outlier (`812.037`, strike and reshoot, never average).
6. **Step 3 the call** — `2436.012 ÷ 3 = 812.004`, `−812.000 = +0.004 → GOOD` next to `+0.013 → GOES BACK`.
7. **The real 16 Jul run**, worked end to end over your page photo.
8. **The quiz** — 812.006 / **812.041** / 812.003, a 5-count, then the reveal.
9. **Rule card** to freeze on.

Everything is in **feet to three places**, every step shows good beside bad, and every number is worked on screen.

**Two things to flag:**
- **The quiz call:** the readings force the call I'm confident you'd make — Set 2 is 0.037 off, so it's a *strike and reshoot, never average*, and the video shows the trap (averaging gives 812.017 → you'd send a good gun back over one bad set). You said you'd dig out your own page — when you do, the script.md marks exactly where to drop it in and the one line in the generator to change. If your page ends on a straight good/goes-back instead, that swaps in the same way.
- I read "back from LEIS" as **Llano Estacado Instrument Service** (matches the sheet letterhead and the Lubbock trip). If that's wrong, it's one line to fix.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Builds baseline_check.mp4 — the office-follow-along video for the baseline check.

Source of truth: Abe's book pages (IMG_4638, IMG_4639), the setup photo (IMG_4452),
and Abe's own mail + calendar (why the S6 went in; how the baseline was established).

Everything on screen is in FEET to three places. No millimetres.

To swap in Abe's own quiz page: edit the QUIZ block near the bottom and re-run:
    python3 make_baseline_video.py
"""

import os
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import imageio.v2 as imageio

IN = "/app/inputs"
OUT = "/app/outputs"
FPS = 30
W, H = 1920, 1080

# ---- palette -------------------------------------------------------------
BG     = (22, 24, 28)
PANEL  = (32, 35, 41)
INK    = (238, 240, 243)
MUTED  = (154, 160, 170)
GOOD   = (60, 196, 124)
BAD    = (230, 88, 80)
ACCENT = (247, 197, 42)   # instrument yellow
LINE   = (72, 76, 86)
GOODBG = (26, 46, 36)
BADBG  = (52, 30, 30)

FONTDIR = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu"
_cache = {}
def font(kind, size):
    key = (kind, size)
    if key not in _cache:
        f = {"sans":"DejaVuSans.ttf","bold":"DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf",
             "mono":"DejaVuSansMono.ttf","monob":"DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf"}[kind]
        _cache[key] = ImageFont.truetype(os.path.join(FONTDIR, f), size)
    return _cache[key]

# ---- draw helpers --------------------------------------------------------
def canvas(bg=BG):
    im = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), bg)
    return im, ImageDraw.Draw(im)

def text(d, xy, s, fnt, fill=INK, anchor="la"):
    d.text(xy, s, font=fnt, fill=fill, anchor=anchor)

def measure(fnt, s):
    return fnt.getlength(s)

def wrap(d, s, fnt, x, y, maxw, fill=INK, leading=1.35, center=False):
    words, lines, cur = s.split(), [], ""
    for w in words:
        t = (cur + " " + w).strip()
        if measure(fnt, t) <= maxw:
            cur = t
        else:
            if cur: lines.append(cur)
            cur = w
    if cur: lines.append(cur)
    lh = int(fnt.size * leading)
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        d.text((x, y+i*lh), ln, font=fnt, fill=fill, anchor=("ma" if center else "la"))
    return y + len(lines)*lh

def panel(d, box, fill=PANEL, outline=None, width=2, radius=22):
    d.rounded_rectangle(box, radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=width)

def chip(d, xy, s, fill, textcol=(15,16,18), fnt=None, pad=(22,12)):
    fnt = fnt or font("bold", 34)
    tw = measure(fnt, s); x, y = xy
    box = (x, y, x+tw+pad[0]*2, y+fnt.size+pad[1]*2)
    d.rounded_rectangle(box, radius=(box[3]-box[1])//2, fill=fill)
    d.text((x+pad[0], y+pad[1]-2), s, font=fnt, fill=textcol)
    return box

def label_masked(d, cx, cy, s, fnt, fill, pad=12, bg=BG):
    """Center a label at (cx, cy top) with a background box so any line behind it stays readable."""
    w = measure(fnt, s)
    d.rectangle((cx-w/2-pad, cy-4, cx+w/2+pad, cy+fnt.size+8), fill=bg)
    d.text((cx, cy), s, font=fnt, fill=fill, anchor="ma")

def footer(d, page=""):
    d.line((90, H-92, W-90, H-92), fill=LINE, width=2)
    text(d, (90, H-70),
         "S6  SN 93441234   •   Baseline BL-1–BL-2  =  812.000 ft   •   feet to three places",
         font("sans", 26), MUTED)
    if page:
        text(d, (W-90, H-70), page, font("bold", 26), MUTED, anchor="ra")

def header(d, kicker, title, tcol=INK):
    text(d, (90, 66), kicker, font("bold", 30), ACCENT)
    # auto-fit title so it never clips the right edge
    size = 72
    while size > 50 and measure(font("bold", size), title) > (W-180):
        size -= 2
    text(d, (90, 114), title, font("bold", size), tcol)
    d.line((90, 210, W-90, 210), fill=LINE, width=3)

def goodbad_headers(d, lx, rx, top, w, badlabel="BAD"):
    d.rounded_rectangle((lx, top, lx+w, top+70), radius=14, fill=GOOD)
    d.rounded_rectangle((rx, top, rx+w, top+70), radius=14, fill=BAD)
    text(d, (lx+w//2, top+8), "GOOD", font("bold", 44), (12,30,20), anchor="ma")
    text(d, (rx+w//2, top+8), badlabel, font("bold", 44), (30,12,12), anchor="ma")

def load_fit(path, box_w, box_h):
    im = Image.open(path).convert("RGB")
    r = min(box_w/im.width, box_h/im.height)
    return im.resize((max(1,int(im.width*r)), max(1,int(im.height*r))), Image.LANCZOS)

SLIDES = []
def add(im, sec, fade=True): SLIDES.append((im, sec, fade))

# =========================================================================
# 0. TITLE
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
d.rectangle((0,0,W,12), fill=ACCENT)
text(d, (W//2, 235), "BASELINE CHECK", font("bold", 128), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (W//2, 388), "The whole thing, start to finish — so anyone can run it without Abe.",
     font("sans", 40), MUTED, anchor="ma")
panel(d, (W//2-580, 500, W//2+580, 770), fill=PANEL, outline=LINE)
text(d, (W//2, 528), "Any instrument back from a bench gets this before it goes out.",
     font("sans", 36), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (W//2, 596), "Tripod both ends.  PPM every time.  Feet to three places.",
     font("bold", 40), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (W//2, 664), "Inside 0.010 ft = good.   Over = it goes back.",
     font("bold", 42), ACCENT, anchor="ma")
text(d, (W//2, 720), "Write it down.", font("bold", 36), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (W//2, 870), "Do the math on the screen, not in a spreadsheet after.",
     font("sans", 34), MUTED, anchor="ma")
add(im, 6.0)

# =========================================================================
# 1. WHERE THE BASELINE CAME FROM
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "FIRST — WHAT YOU ARE STANDING ON", "Where our baseline came from")
wrap(d, "Abe set two brass caps behind the shop at 8710 Bowie in 2016 — 812.000 ft apart, with "
        "the midpoint 406.000 out. He re-observes the line every spring to hold the 812.000. It is "
        "our own baseline, and that 812.000 is the truth we judge against.",
     font("sans", 38), 90, 244, W-180, MUTED)

y = 590
x1, x2 = 220, W-220
xm = (x1+x2)//2
d.line((x1, y, x2, y), fill=INK, width=6)
for x, lab, sub in [(x1,"BL-1","0.000"),(xm,"BL-M","406.000"),(x2,"BL-2","812.000")]:
    d.line((x, y-34, x, y+34), fill=ACCENT, width=8)
    text(d, (x, y-96), lab, font("bold", 46), INK, anchor="ma")
    text(d, (x, y+52), sub, font("mono", 34), MUTED, anchor="ma")
d.line((x1, y+150, xm, y+150), fill=LINE, width=3)
d.line((xm, y+150, x2, y+150), fill=LINE, width=3)
label_masked(d, (x1+xm)//2, y+134, "406.000", font("mono", 30), MUTED)
label_masked(d, (xm+x2)//2, y+134, "406.000", font("mono", 30), MUTED)
d.line((x1, y+238, x2, y+238), fill=ACCENT, width=4)
label_masked(d, xm, y+214, "812.000 ft  —  our hold since 2016", font("bold", 40), ACCENT)
text(d, (xm, y+292), "Two brass caps, set 2016  ·  re-observed every spring  ·  NOT the brochure.",
     font("sans", 30), INK, anchor="ma")
footer(d, "1 / 9")
add(im, 9.0)

# =========================================================================
# 2. WHY THE S6 WENT IN  (the story)
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "WHY THE S6 WENT IN", "What happened on 26-004")
steps = [
    ("2 Jun", "Deaf Smith County — the 640-acre pivot as-builts, job 26-004. Estefana on the rod."),
    ("",      "The S6 lost the tracker at 2:20 and would not re-acquire. We finished the day on the R12i and a 100-ft tape."),
    ("3 Jun", "Drove it to Llano Estacado Instrument Service in Lubbock. Talmadge Ruff opened it up: tracker board and Y servo. Six weeks on the bench."),
    ("16 Jul","Back four days early, sheet in the case."),
]
yy = 250
for when, what in steps:
    if when:
        chip(d, (90, yy), when, ACCENT, fnt=font("bold", 30))
    yy2 = wrap(d, what, font("sans", 38), 330, yy+6, W-420, INK)
    yy = max(yy2, yy+90) + 14

panel(d, (90, 800, W-90, 900), fill=(44,38,24), outline=ACCENT, width=2, radius=16)
text(d, (W//2, 820), "A bench can say it's fixed. The baseline is how WE know —",
     font("bold", 36), ACCENT, anchor="ma")
text(d, (W//2, 862), "before it goes back out on a job.", font("bold", 36), ACCENT, anchor="ma")
footer(d, "2 / 9")
add(im, 11.0)

# =========================================================================
# 3. SETUP  (good vs bad) — center, level, both ends, constant
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "SET UP THE SAME WAY EVERY TIME", "Set up both ends")
photo = load_fit(os.path.join(IN, "IMG_4452.jpg"), 820, 600)
im.paste(photo, (90, 252))
text(d, (90, 252+photo.height+10), "Abe's setup behind the shop.", font("sans", 26), MUTED)

gx, gw = 960, 880
bf = font("sans", 30)
d.rounded_rectangle((gx, 250, gx+gw, 318), radius=14, fill=GOOD)
text(d, (gx+gw//2, 258), "GOOD", font("bold", 40), (12,30,20), anchor="ma")
panel(d, (gx, 326, gx+gw, 600), fill=GOODBG, outline=GOOD, width=2)
for i,s in enumerate([
    "Instrument on a tripod over BL-1, legs firm.",
    "Center over the cap, then level.",
    "Prism on a tripod over BL-2, both level.",
    "Trimble 360 prism, constant 0.0."]):
    text(d, (gx+30, 352+i*60), "•  "+s, bf, INK)

d.rounded_rectangle((gx, 620, gx+gw, 688), radius=14, fill=BAD)
text(d, (gx+gw//2, 628), "BAD", font("bold", 40), (30,12,12), anchor="ma")
panel(d, (gx, 696, gx+gw, 966), fill=BADBG, outline=BAD, width=2)
for i,s in enumerate([
    "Prism on a hand pole — it rocks.",
    "Legs loose — the tripod walks.",
    "Off-center or off-level — reads off.",
    "Constant wrong — same bias every shot."]):
    text(d, (gx+30, 722+i*60), "•  "+s, bf, INK)
footer(d, "3 / 9")
add(im, 10.0)

# =========================================================================
# 4. STEP 1 - PPM  (title short; arithmetic clear of footer)
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "STEP 1 — BEFORE THE FIRST SHOT, EVERY TIME", "PPM off the shop gauge")
wrap(d, "Read the shop gauge. Punch temperature and pressure into the S6 so it sets PPM. "
        "Forget it and the S6 reads short.",
     font("sans", 38), 90, 244, W-180, MUTED)

lx, rx, w, top = 120, 1030, 760, 388
goodbad_headers(d, lx, rx, top, w)
panel(d, (lx, top+80, lx+w, top+360), fill=GOODBG, outline=GOOD, width=2)
panel(d, (rx, top+80, rx+w, top+360), fill=BADBG, outline=BAD, width=2)
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+104), "97°F   26.40 inHg   →  PPM +52", font("mono", 32), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+170), "812.005", font("monob", 90), GOOD, anchor="ma")
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+300), "PPM set. Reads true.", font("sans", 32), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (rx+w//2, top+104), "PPM left at 0   (forgot it)", font("mono", 32), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (rx+w//2, top+170), "811.962", font("monob", 90), BAD, anchor="ma")
text(d, (rx+w//2, top+300), "Struck in July. Set PPM, shot again.", font("sans", 30), INK, anchor="ma")

ay = 838   # arithmetic strip well above footer line at H-92 (=988)
panel(d, (120, ay, W-120, ay+110), fill=PANEL, outline=LINE)
text(d, (150, ay+16), "On the screen:", font("bold", 28), ACCENT)
text(d, (150, ay+56), "812.000 ft × 0.000052 = 0.042 ft short   812.005 − 811.962 = 0.043 ft",
     font("mono", 34), INK)
footer(d, "4 / 9")
add(im, 9.0)

# =========================================================================
# 5. STEP 2 - THREE SETS + spread rule (good vs bad)
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "STEP 2", "Three sets, HD, feet — check the spread")
wrap(d, "Shoot three sets of horizontal distance. A set more than 0.005 off the other two is a "
        "strike (a bump, or PPM). Strike it, shoot it again. Never average a strike.",
     font("sans", 38), 90, 244, W-180, MUTED)
lx, rx, w, top = 120, 1030, 760, 440
goodbad_headers(d, lx, rx, top, w)
panel(d, (lx, top+80, lx+w, top+460), fill=GOODBG, outline=GOOD, width=2)
panel(d, (rx, top+80, rx+w, top+460), fill=BADBG, outline=BAD, width=2)
for i,(lab,val) in enumerate([("Set 1","812.005"),("Set 2","812.003"),("Set 3","812.004")]):
    text(d, (lx+40, top+108+i*70), lab, font("sans", 36), MUTED)
    text(d, (lx+300, top+108+i*70), val, font("mono", 46), INK)
text(d, (lx+40, top+328), "spread = 0.002  (≤ 0.005)", font("mono", 34), GOOD)
text(d, (lx+40, top+388), "Keep all three.", font("bold", 36), GOOD)
for i,(lab,val,c) in enumerate([("Set 1","812.004",INK),("Set 2","812.037",BAD),("Set 3","812.003",INK)]):
    text(d, (rx+40, top+108+i*70), lab, font("sans", 36), MUTED)
    text(d, (rx+300, top+108+i*70), val, font("mono", 46), c)
text(d, (rx+40, top+328), "Set 2 is 0.033 off  (> 0.005)", font("mono", 34), BAD)
text(d, (rx+40, top+388), "Strike Set 2. Reshoot. Don't average.", font("bold", 30), BAD)
footer(d, "5 / 9")
add(im, 9.0)

# =========================================================================
# 6. STEP 3 - MEAN & CALL (good vs bad)
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "STEP 3", "Mean of three, less 812.000 — make the call")
wrap(d, "Add the three good sets, divide by three, subtract 812.000. Inside 0.010 ft is good. "
        "Over, it goes back. Tight sets can still fail — do the math.",
     font("sans", 38), 90, 244, W-180, MUTED)
lx, rx, w, top = 120, 1030, 760, 430
goodbad_headers(d, lx, rx, top, w)
panel(d, (lx, top+80, lx+w, top+470), fill=GOODBG, outline=GOOD, width=2)
panel(d, (rx, top+80, rx+w, top+470), fill=BADBG, outline=BAD, width=2)
text(d, (lx+40, top+96), "S6 · 16 Jul · after repair", font("sans", 26), MUTED)
text(d, (lx+40, top+134), "812.005 + 812.003 + 812.004", font("mono", 32), INK)
text(d, (lx+40, top+184), "= 2436.012  ÷ 3  = 812.004", font("mono", 32), INK)
text(d, (lx+40, top+244), "812.004 − 812.000 = +0.004", font("mono", 36), INK)
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+324), "+0.004  ≤  0.010", font("monob", 48), GOOD, anchor="ma")
chip(d, (lx+w//2-95, top+382), "GOOD", GOOD)
text(d, (rx+40, top+96), "S6 · 18 Apr · before it went in", font("sans", 26), MUTED)
text(d, (rx+40, top+134), "812.012 + 812.015 + 812.012", font("mono", 32), INK)
text(d, (rx+40, top+184), "= 2436.039  ÷ 3  = 812.013", font("mono", 32), INK)
text(d, (rx+40, top+244), "812.013 − 812.000 = +0.013", font("mono", 36), INK)
text(d, (rx+w//2, top+324), "+0.013  >  0.010", font("monob", 48), BAD, anchor="ma")
chip(d, (rx+w//2-150, top+382), "IT GOES BACK", BAD)
footer(d, "6 / 9")
add(im, 9.0)

# =========================================================================
# 6b. WHY NOT TALMADGE'S NUMBER  (Estefana's question)
# =========================================================================
im, d = canvas()
header(d, "ESTEFANA'S QUESTION", "Why not just use Talmadge's number?")
wrap(d, "His sheet certifies the gun on a 3-pillar bench: ±(2 mm + 2 ppm). Work that at our "
        "812.000 ft and set it beside the office limit.",
     font("sans", 38), 90, 244, W-180, MUTED)
lx, rx, w, top = 120, 1030, 760, 400
# left — the brochure allowance
d.rounded_rectangle((lx, top, lx+w, top+70), radius=14, fill=LINE)
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+8), "TALMADGE'S SHEET", font("bold", 40), INK, anchor="ma")
panel(d, (lx, top+80, lx+w, top+440), fill=PANEL, outline=LINE, width=2)
text(d, (lx+30, top+106), "±(2 mm + 2 ppm), prism mode", font("mono", 30), INK)
text(d, (lx+30, top+156), "worked at our 812.000 ft:", font("sans", 28), MUTED)
text(d, (lx+30, top+212), "2 mm             → 0.007 ft", font("mono", 30), INK)
text(d, (lx+30, top+260), "2 ppm × 812.000  → 0.002 ft", font("mono", 30), INK)
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+338), "the pair  →  ±0.008 ft", font("monob", 44), INK, anchor="ma")
text(d, (lx+w//2, top+400), "(each rounded to 0.001 ft)", font("sans", 22), MUTED, anchor="ma")
# right — the office limit

# Baseline Check — Script & Procedure

**Instrument this was built for:** Trimble S6, SN 93441234
**The line:** BL-1 → BL-2 behind the shop (8710 Bowie), **812.000 ft**, midpoint monument **BL-M at 406.000**
**The rule, in one line:** mean of three sets less 812.000 — **inside 0.010 ft = good, over = it goes back.**

> **Print this and keep it in the case.** It matches the video `baseline_check.mp4` step for step.
> Whoever runs the check reads this; the video shows them what it looks like.
> Everything is in **feet to three places**. Nobody here reads millimetres.

---

## When you run this

Any time an instrument comes back onto the property from a bench — repair, service,
calibration, anywhere off-site — it gets this check **before it goes back out on a job.**
Abe ran the S6 the same afternoon it came back from Lubbock. Same for everything else.

**The sheet that came back in the case is nice to have. The sheet is not the check.**
The baseline is the check.

---

## What you need

- The instrument that came back, on a **tripod**.
- Prism on a **tripod** at the far monument. **Never a hand-held pole** — a pole rocks and every set moves.
- Trimble 360 prism, prism constant **0.0**.
- The shop weather gauge (temperature + pressure).
- The check page and a pen. Write the readings down as you go.

---

## The video, section by section (narration)

Read it in this order if you ever need to walk someone through it without the screen.

### 0 · Title
"This is the baseline check, start to finish, so anyone can run it without Abe. Any instrument
back from a bench gets it before it goes out. Tripod both ends, PPM every time, feet to three
places. Inside 0.010 is good, over goes back. Write it down. Do the math on the screen."

### 1 · Where our baseline came from
"Abe set **two brass caps** behind the shop at 8710 Bowie in **2016** — **812.000 ft** apart, with
the midpoint 406.000 out (BL-M). He **re-observes the line every spring** to hold the 812.000.
It's our own baseline, and that 812.000 is the truth we judge against. **Not the brochure.**"

### 2 · Why the S6 went in (the story)
- **2 Jun** — Deaf Smith County, the 640-acre pivot as-builts, **job 26-004**. Estefana on the rod.
- The **S6 lost the tracker at 2:20 and would not re-acquire.** We finished the day on the R12i and a 100-ft tape.
- **3 Jun** — drove it to **Llano Estacado Instrument Service** in Lubbock. Talmadge Ruff opened it up: **tracker board and Y servo.** Six weeks on the bench.
- **16 Jul** — back four days early, sheet in the case.

"A bench can say it's fixed. **The baseline is how we know** — before it goes back out on a job."

### 3 · Set up both ends

| GOOD | BAD |
|---|---|
| Instrument on a tripod over BL-1, legs kicked in firm. | Prism on a hand pole — it rocks, every set moves. |
| Center over the monument, then level (tribrach + comp). | Legs loose — the tripod walks between sets. |
| Prism on a tripod over BL-2. Both tribrachs level. | Off-center or off-level — reads long or short. |
| Trimble 360 prism, constant **0.0**. | Constant left wrong — same bias on every shot. |

### 4 · Step 1 — PPM off the shop gauge, before the first shot
Read the shop gauge. Punch temperature and pressure into the instrument so it sets PPM. **Every time.**

| | GOOD | BAD |
|---|---|---|
| gauge | 97°F, 26.40 inHg → **PPM +52** | **PPM left at 0** (forgot it) |
| reads | **812.005** | **811.962** |

**On the screen:** `812.000 ft × 0.000052 = 0.042 ft short` and `812.005 − 811.962 = 0.043 ft`.
Forget PPM and the instrument reads short by about that much. (This is the shot Abe struck in July,
then set PPM and shot again.)

### 5 · Step 2 — three sets, HD, feet — check the spread
Shoot **three sets** of horizontal distance.

- **GOOD:** 812.005 / 812.003 / 812.004 → spread **0.002** (≤ 0.005). Keep all three.
- **BAD:** 812.004 / **812.037** / 812.003 → Set 2 is **0.033 off** (> 0.005). That's a strike
  (a bump, or PPM). **Strike it, shoot it again. Never average a strike.**

### 6 · Step 3 — mean of three, less 812.000 — make the call
Add the three good sets, divide by three, subtract 812.000.

- **GOOD — S6, 16 Jul, after repair:** `812.005 + 812.003 + 812.004 = 2436.012 ÷ 3 = 812.004`;
  `812.004 − 812.000 = +0.004`. **+0.004 ≤ 0.010 → GOOD, it stays.**
- **BAD — S6, 18 Apr, before it went in** (64°F, 26.70, PPM +35): `812.012 + 812.015 + 812.012 =
  2436.039 ÷ 3 = 812.013`; `812.013 − 812.000 = +0.013`. **+0.013 > 0.010 → IT GOES BACK.**
  (Tracker was hunting on set 2 — the spring check first flagged it: "call Talmadge, it does it again."
  It finally went in after it quit on the pivot job on 2 Jun, dropped at Llano on 3 Jun.)

### Why not just use Talmadge's number? (Estefana's question)
His service sheet certifies the instrument on his 3-pillar bench: **±(2 mm + 2 ppm)**, prism mode.
Worked at our baseline length, in feet to three places:

- 2 mm → **0.007 ft** (the fixed part — exactly 0.0066 ft)
- 2 ppm × 812.000 ft → **0.002 ft** (the scale part — exactly 0.0016 ft)
- together → **±0.008 ft** (0.0082 ft, rounded to three places)

**Office limit: ±0.010 ft.**

**We use 0.010 — the office limit.** It's a field limit for the *whole setup on our line* — tripods
both ends, tribrachs, centering, PPM, and the baseline itself — not the instrument alone on
Talmadge's bench. His sheet is nice to have; the baseline against 0.010 ft is the check.

### 7 · Write the check down
Same page every time, in the case. Don't trust your memory.

**GOOD — the whole check on the page:**
```
16 Jul 26   S6 93441234
BL-1-BL-2   812.000
97F  26.40  PPM +52
1  812.005
2  812.003
3  812.004
mean 812.004   +0.004
GOOD - stays        AIQ
```

**BAD — useless to Estefana in a year:**
```
S6   93441234
(no ppm noted)
812.005  812.037  812.003
avg 812.015   ~ok
```
No date. No PPM. Averaged a strike (the 812.037). +0.015 is over 0.010 — wrong call.

### 8 · The real run — 16 Jul
- Back from Lubbock. Tripod both ends. 97°F, 26.40 → PPM +52.
- First shot PPM was 0 → **811.962. Struck it.** Set PPM, shot again:
  - Set 1 **812.005**
  - Set 2 **812.003**
  - Set 3 **812.004**
- Mean **812.004**. `812.004 − 812.000 = +0.004`. **+0.004 ≤ 0.010 → GOOD, it stays.**

---

## The quiz — call it before the video does

On screen: **Abe's 22 Jun page for the loaner S5 (SN 30712216) from Llano** — checked before it
went out on a job. The arithmetic and the call are cut off the bottom **on purpose**. Watch the
page, take **ten seconds**, then work it and call it.

**What's on the page:**
- Published **812.000** · tripod both ends
- 88°F, 26.55 → **PPM +47**
- Set 1 — **812.008**
- Set 2 — 812.031 → *leg in the sand* — struck and reshot → **812.010**
- Set 3 — **812.009**

**Work it on the screen:**
```
812.008 + 812.010 + 812.009 = 2436.027 ÷ 3 = 812.009
812.009 − 812.000 = +0.009
```

**The call:** **+0.009 ≤ 0.010 → GOOD. The loaner goes out.**
Inside 0.010 by a hair — still good. And Set 2 was struck for the leg in the sand and reshot,
never averaged. Write it down: 22 Jun, S5, PPM +47, the three sets, mean 812.009, +0.009, GOOD.

> The page image (`baseline_quiz_page.jpg`) sits alongside this script and in the video. To use a
> different page later, replace that image and the three sets / worked call above, then rebuild the
> video: `python3 make_baseline_video.py`.

---

## The rule card (keep in the case)

1. Any instrument back from a bench gets this **before** it goes out.
2. BL-1 to BL-2 = **812.000 ft**, set 2016, re-observed every spring. Tripod both ends, never a pole.
3. Set up both ends: **center, level, prism constant 0.0.**
4. **PPM off the shop gauge before the first shot. Every time.**
5. **Three sets, HD, feet.**
6. A set **> 0.005** off the other two = **strike it, shoot it again. Never average.**
7. Mean of three, less 812.000:
   - inside **0.010 ft → GOOD**
   - over **0.010 ft → IT GOES BACK**
8. **Write it down:** date, gun, conditions, PPM, three sets, mean, the call, initials.
9. Judge against **812.000** and our **±0.010 ft**. **Not the brochure** — its ±(2 mm + 2 ppm) is only ≈ ±0.008 ft at our length, and it's the gun alone on the bench.

*For Estefana, and whoever comes after. — Abe*

The service sheet spec is **±(2 mm + 2 ppm)**, prism mode. Worked at 812.000 ft that is **≈ ±0.008 ft**

Our **±0.010 ft** is a field limit that covers the whole setup on our line — tripods both ends,
tribrachs, centering, PPM, and the baseline itself. **Judge against 0.010 ft. Not the brochure.**
